en.name: Red seabream
en.summary: Red seabream, madai, is the celebratory fish of Japanese and Taiwanese tables — lean, firm and pale pink under a red skin. Fresh it keeps 1–2 days in the fridge and 6–8 months in the freezer, but eat it raw only on the day it is cut.
en.pantry: Sea bream has no room-temperature life. It is a lean fish, so it has no fat to buffer it, and the firm texture that makes it good for sashimi is the first thing warmth takes away. Bring it home cold, and follow the 2-hour rule, or 1 hour if it is above 32 °C (90 °F). Do not leave a whole fish out while you find a pan big enough.
en.fridge: Scale and gut it before chilling — ask the stall to do it — then hold it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below on ice, in a container that catches the melt water, and cook it within 1–2 days. If you are eating it raw, buy fish sold for raw eating, keep it on ice at the bottom of the fridge, and eat it on the day it is cut; raw fish is not advised for pregnant, elderly, very young or immunocompromised people. Store it below anything ready to eat. A whole fish holds better than fillets, and the head and collar are worth keeping for soup.
en.freezer: Red seabream keeps 6–8 months at −18 °C (0 °F), a long window because there is so little fat to oxidise. What freezing costs is the firm, slightly crisp texture prized for sashimi, so freeze only fish you plan to cook. Wrap fillets airtight with no air pockets or ice-glaze them by dipping in cold water, and freeze flat in portions. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the months are about quality.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge overnight on a plate, or in a sealed bag under cold running water. Never on the counter or in warm water. Cook it promptly and do not refreeze raw fish.
spoilage: A sour or ammoniacal smell instead of a clean, faintly sweet one.
Flesh that stays dented when pressed rather than springing back.
Cloudy sunken eyes and grey-brown gills on a whole fish.
Skin that has lost its red gloss and gone dull and slimy.
tips: Have it scaled and gutted at the stall.
Keep the head and collar for soup; they are the best part for stock.
Eat it raw only on the day it is cut, and only if it was sold for raw eating.
Freeze only the portions you intend to cook.

faq.q: How long does sea bream keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 1–2 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, scaled, gutted and on ice.
Yes, 6–8 months at −18 °C. It is lean and freezes well, but it loses the firm texture that suits sashimi, so freeze it for cooking.

faq.q: How long can you keep sea bream for sashimi?
faq.a: Eat it raw on the day it is cut, and only if it was sold for raw eating and kept cold throughout.

faq.q: How can you tell if sea bream has gone off?
faq.a: A sour or ammoniacal smell, dull slimy skin, cloudy sunken eyes, or flesh that will not spring back.

zh.name: 真鯛
zh.summary: 真鯛是日本與台灣餐桌上的喜慶魚，肉質低脂結實、呈淡粉色，外皮紅亮。新鮮的冷藏可放 1～2 天，冷凍 6～8 個月；但要生食，只限切開當天。
zh.pantry: 鯛魚沒有室溫保存這回事。它是低脂魚，沒有脂肪當緩衝，而讓它適合做生魚片的那種結實口感，正是溫度最先奪走的東西。請保冷帶回家，並守 2 小時原則，室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。不要一邊找夠大的鍋、一邊把整條魚放在檯面上。
zh.fridge: 冷藏前先去鱗去內臟——請攤商代勞——然後鋪冰放 4 °C 以下，容器要能接住融水，並在 1～2 天內煮掉。要生食的話，請買標示可生食的魚貨，鋪冰放冰箱最下層，並在切開當天吃完；生魚不建議孕婦、長者、幼童與免疫力低下者食用。位置要低於所有即食食品。整條比魚片耐放，而且魚頭和下巴留著煮湯非常值得。
zh.freezer: 真鯛在 −18 °C 下可放 6～8 個月，區間長是因為幾乎沒有會氧化的脂肪。冷凍會犧牲的是做生魚片時那種結實微脆的口感，所以只冷凍你打算煮熟的部分。魚片密封包好不留空氣，或浸冷水做冰鍍，分裝壓平。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，月數講的是品質。
zh.thawing: 放盤子上冷藏隔夜解凍，或密封裝袋用冷水沖。不要放室溫或泡溫水。解凍後盡快烹調，生魚不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 聞起來發酸或有氨味，而不是乾淨帶淡甜的魚味。
按壓後凹陷回不來，而不是有彈性。
整條魚眼睛混濁凹陷、魚鰓轉灰褐。
魚皮失去紅亮光澤，變得黯淡黏滑。
tips: 請攤商當場去鱗去內臟。
魚頭和下巴留著煮湯，那是熬湯最好的部位。
要生食只限切開當天，而且必須是標示可生食的魚貨。
只冷凍你打算煮熟的那幾份。

faq.a: 去鱗去內臟、鋪冰放 4 °C 以下，1～2 天。
可以，−18 °C 下 6～8 個月。它低脂、很耐凍，但會失去適合生魚片的結實口感，所以冷凍的部分請煮熟吃。

faq.q: 要做生魚片的鯛魚可以放多久？
faq.a: 只限切開當天，而且必須是標示可生食、全程低溫的魚貨。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷鯛魚不新鮮了？
faq.a: 發酸或氨味、魚皮黯淡發黏、眼睛混濁凹陷，或按壓沒有彈性。
